messages:
jia: Quick heads-up — while stress-testing long-context replay (200k tokens) on H100 we see persistent GPU memory growth even after eviction runs. Seems tied to page-table churn + small-page fragmentation. Repro attached below.
alex: hmm. is this the paged-kv path or new compacting allocator?
maria: which kernel path are you hitting? nvcc/compiler differences can change allocator behavior on H100 vs A100.
jia: PagedKV path (PagedAttention-style). Kernel selection differs: H100 picks the 'vec' fused-kernel for attention in some shapes, A100 picks the baseline. I profiled and noticed much higher page-table entry churn on H100.
sam: can you paste the nvprof / metrics output? numbers help.
jia: Sure — trimmed: 
```
GPU: H100
run #4 (steady state): resident: 45.2GB -> 48.9GB (+3.7GB over 10k steps)
page_table_entries: 128k -> 412k
evictions/sec: 320 -> 1280
avg_page_util: 0.42
kernel: attention_vec_fused, batch_size=8, seq=4096
```
alex: evictions/sec spiking with page_table_entries rising suggests lots of tiny frees/allocs — fragmentation. Are pages variable-sized?
jia: pages are power-of-two buckets but we have mixed sizes (4KB, 64KB, 1MB) due to KV cache slice splitting. When the fused kernel changes access pattern, reuse locality drops.
maria: I bet the kernel's parallel read pattern is holding references across streams while eviction frees pages on another stream — possible ABA or delayed CUDA event sync. Any cudaStreamSynchronize or event wait in evict path?
jia: Evict path schedules frees on background stream and uses events to mark completion, but I found an intermittent window where free_list node gets recycled while a read still in-flight. No crash, but we see "ghost" pages counted in PT but not reclaimed — memory accounting leak.
sam: Can you share minimal repro? maybe we can toggle concurrent evictions off.
jia: Repro gist (pseudo):
```
for i in range(10000):
  ctx = gen_context(window=4096 * i % 3)
  out = model.infer(ctx, kv_paging=True)
  if i % 50 == 0:
    scheduler.trigger_eviction(async=True)
```
Run with env: RWD_KV_PAGE_SIZE=65536, RWD_KV_BACKGROUND_STREAM=1.
Observed: on H100 leak persists, on A100 smaller but still present at higher rate. On 4090 consumer GPU no leak (likely different driver/kernel behavior).
alex: That points to driver/arch sensitivity. Could also be alignment of page mappings causing more fragmentation on H100. Two things to try: 1) force synchronous frees (background_stream=0) 2) change allocator to coalesce adjacent free pages.
jia: I tried disabling bg_stream (set to 0) — growth stops but throughput drops ~8%. So it's an integration bug with async free.
maria: Forcing coalescing might help; but we should also add debug asserts to ensure no outstanding refs when we put page on free_list. Add an epoch counter per page and increment on read, decrement on free and assert zero.
sam: Also add counters: PT.total_pages_live, PT.total_pages_free_list_len, PT.shadow_ref_count. Compare across runs.
jia: Added counters — pattern: free_list length grows unexpectedly then shrinks, but PT.total_pages_live never goes down. Looks like the free_list returns pages but PT keeps ghost entries because page-table unmap failed on one codepath (race).
alex: Could be missing cudaEventRecord before unmap confirmation. Race where unmap scheduled but not waited on before PT mark removed. Add explicit event.wait in unmap path.
maria: Another angle: kernel selection might change memory access ordering so a reader holds a stale device pointer that keeps a page resident even after free; we might be leaking dangling device-mapped memory. Use cudaMemRangeGetAttributes? or track cudaPointerGetAttributes to debug.
infra-bot: test-run completed: 1774123468 — h100-repro-evict-off: peak_resident=45.4GB, steady=45.5GB; h100-repro-default: peak_resident=49.1GB, steady=48.9GB.
sam: Good. Action items: 1) add stronger sync in unmap/freetable path (try for canary) 2) incrementally enable coalescing allocator in nightly 3) add per-page epoch/ref assertions behind a low-overhead flag 4) run matrix on A100/H100/RTX4090.
jia: I'll open a PR with a canary patch for synchronous unmap (toggle via env RWD_KV_STRICT_UNMAP=1) and add the ref counters. Posting logs in the PR.
alex: When you open PR, include microbench that measures throughput delta and memory numbers. Also check kernel selection fallback — maybe force the baseline attention kernel on H100 to see if behavior changes.
maria: If strict unmap fixes leak, we can later optimize by inserting cudaStreamWaitEvent to safe points instead of full sync.
sam: I'll schedule perf jobs across clouds (gcp a100, gcp h100, local 4090) and add results to the ticket.
jia: Thanks — will follow up with PR link and test matrix. :bug: :thinking_face:
